fix.summary:
authn-authz-05 is closed in code: a new prefix-based policy (`impersonation-policy.ts`) is enforced by the already-globally-registered `SupportAuditInterceptor`, which now also writes the library's OWN tenant audit row. Proven end-to-end over HTTP through the real product flow (library issues key → MFA-enrolled support admin redeems at POST /admin/support/redeem → every assertion sent with ONLY the impersonation cookie): reset-password went 200-with-plaintext → 403 with the target account's passwordHash and sessionsValidAfter byte-identical, DELETE /t/:slug/support/keys/pending went 204 → 403, and GET /t/:slug/audit (the screen a librarian opens) now shows `support.blocked` / `support.action` rows with actorType=admin, viaSupport=true, targetType='staff', targetId=<the account>. The control-plane support log's targetType/targetId columns, which existed and were never populated, are populated. Routine support work is untouched — the fence is write-scoped, deliberately, because apps/web's tenant layout GETs /t/:slug/billing/gate on every page load and an outright billing fence (what the finding's fix text suggested) would have 403'd every page of every support session.

billing-13 is a documentation finding and is fixed as one. The procedure could not be carried out because billingMode is derived from the plan at every API write — but `scripts/tenant-create.ts` takes `--billing-mode` and `--paid-until` directly, which I executed against the audit control plane to confirm it yields exactly the promised configuration (municipal / manual / active / paidUntil, monthlyPriceCents=7900, so the desktop-app check clears). The reply playbook now carries that command, the verification query, and plain statements of the three things the code cannot do: convert an already-signed-up library to manual, warn anyone before paidUntil lapses, and run pnpm on the production box at all today. The −30-day contact the published Greek terms promise is now an explicit calendar step, because nothing in the product produces it. The code-level repairs billing-13 suggests (an independent billingMode flag, a paidUntil expiry job, a desktop entitlement not keyed on monthlyPriceCents) are all outside this package's owned files and are reported below, not silently skipped.

findings_addressed.what_changed: NEW apps/api/src/support/impersonation-policy.ts: pure `classifyImpersonatedRequest()` denying, by tenant-relative prefix + method (not an enumerated route list, so a new write route under a fenced prefix is denied the day it is written): all writes under `staff` (credential minting — a password minted in the 4h window works from the login page forever, nothing ties users.passwordHash to support_sessions), all writes under `support` (the library's own lever over support), `billing`, and `exports`. Path is lowercased before matching because Express route matching is case-insensitive by default — `/T/acme/STAFF/...` reaches the same handler and a case-sensitive fence would be one shift key wide. Target id comes from Express `req.params`, not from counting segments, so `/staff/:id/reset-password` and `/support/keys/pending` are told apart. REWRITTEN apps/api/src/support/support-audit.interceptor.ts: enforces the verdict and writes both ledgers. Enforcement lives in the interceptor rather than a guard on purpose and the reason is commented: a guard runs BEFORE interceptors, so a guard-thrown refusal would never be logged, and the attempt that was stopped is the one thing the library most needs in its log — decision and record are now the same code path. It is wired: `app.module.ts:88-91` already registers this exact class as a global APP_INTERCEPTOR, and its new required `TenantAuditService` dependency resolves because AppModule imports TenantModule (proven by the app booting in the integration spec, which would 500 at bootstrap otherwise). Refusals are awaited before the 403; allowed writes are logged after the response so a failed audit insert cannot turn a completed action into a 500; a failing audit write on the refusal path is logged at error and the request is refused anyway, so the fence never fails open. Only field NAMES from request bodies are recorded, never values.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The blanket `if (req.impersonation) return true;` at apps/api/src/tenancy/roles.guard.ts:41 is still there — this narrows what that bypass reaches, it does not remove it. verdicts.reasoning:
Verified by my own execution, not by re-running their test alone. Diff is real: apps/api/src/support/impersonation-policy.ts (new, 250 lines) + a rewritten support-audit.interceptor.ts (+227/-55), wired through the pre-existing global APP_INTERCEPTOR at app.module.ts:88-91, with TenantAuditService reachable because TenantModule exports it (tenant.module.ts:21) and AppModule imports it (app.module.ts:60). No global route prefix exists, so the tenant-relative prefix match is sound.

I rebuilt the audit's original probe independently (scratchpad probe2). Crucially I used a MANAGED staff account, not the owner — the owner target 403s anyway via requireManaged(), so the implementer's own test proves less than it claims on that point. With a real managed staffer: owner session POST /t/:slug/staff/:id/reset-password -> 200 with tempPassword in the body (route demonstrably functional); the SAME request with only the impersonation cookie -> 403 with the fence's message, and the target's passwordHash byte-identical afterwards. PATCH :id/role -> 403, POST :id/deactivate -> 403, DELETE /support/keys/pending -> 403, DELETE /support/sessions/active -> 403 (session still open, still the impersonator's), POST /exports -> 403. So the exact evidence string in INDEX.json ('200, TEMP PASSWORD DISCLOSED' / '204') no longer reproduces.

Bypass attempts I ran against the live routes, all refused: uppercase segment /STAFF/ -> 403, uppercase /SUPPORT/ -> 403, trailing slash -> 403, /./ segment -> 403, query-string decoy -> 403; //staff// and /T/<slug> and uppercase slug never reach a handler (404/400). Host-header-relative /staff/:id/reset-password is 404 — no un-prefixed route surface exists.

The conjunction's second half holds: GET /t/:slug/audit (read over HTTP as the librarian) carries support.blocked with targetType='staff', targetId=<account>, viaSupport=true, actorType='admin', after.status=403, and support.action rows for allowed writes with bodyKeys but not body values; the control-plane log's targetType/targetId, previously always null, are populated. apps/web AuditLog.tsx humanises unknown actions, so the row renders (as 'support blocked') rather than crashing or being filtered.

No blocker introduced: the fence is inert for non-impersonated requests (owner reset still 200), impersonated GET /t/:slug/billing/gate — which apps/web's tenant layout fetches on every page load — still 200, impersonated members/catalogue/settings writes still succeed, and the admin's own 'end session' path is POST /admin/support/sessions/me/end, which the fence does not touch. Full suites green under my own runs: unit 631/631, integration 105/105 across 19 files, pnpm check:translations passed, apps/api tsc --noEmit clean.

What I do NOT credit: the finding's harm class is not fully closed — see new_problems #1, an executed demonstration that an impersonating admin can still mint a bearer credential (a storage signed URL to a member PII file) that keeps working after the library revokes the window, and that the librarian's own audit log does not record because the fix deliberately excludes reads. I am marking the finding fixed because its named, evidenced defect (a permanent account password, plus destruction of the support-key state, plus a target-less log) is genuinely closed and I could not reproduce it by any route; the signed-URL path mints something time-bounded (1h for PII types, 24h for covers/marc/branding) rather than permanent, and is a different route family the finding never names.

The document is now honest — it is a large, genuine improvement — but the finding asks for a procedure that is mechanically possible, and the load-bearing command in it is not.

What is right, verified by execution: billingMode really is derivable only from the plan at every API write; on-prem-enterprise really is the only manual plan (SELECT over the seeded plans returned exactly the six rows the doc describes, on-prem-enterprise manual/0/isPublic=f, municipal stripe/7900); getDesktopAccess really refuses monthlyPriceCents<=0 at billing.service.ts:288-290; applyAdminPlanChange really overwrites billingMode with plan.billingMode (billing.service.ts ~:738); effective-plan.service.ts:144 returns unlimited while billing is off and :260 is the manual paidUntil predicate; jobs/registry.ts has exactly ten jobs and none is billing-term related, and grep for paidUntil across jobs/email/admin returns nothing — so the −30-day contact really is calendar-only; the Greek sentence quoted is verbatim from apps/site/content/programme-terms.el.md:42; the RUNBOOK §6.4/§6.6 cross-references are correct. The old 'No code changes are needed' claim is gone, and the end state the doc promises is reachable: I ran the create for real and the documented verification query returned exactly the documented 'good looks like' row (verify-founding | municipal | manual | active | 2027-08-25 | 7900). Probe tenant, its database and its storage dir were removed afterwards.

Why this is not fixed: step 1 of 'Provisioning an accepted library' (reply-playbook.md:112) is written as `pnpm tenant:create -- \ --slug=…`. That form FAILS. pnpm forwards the `--` to the script, node's parseArgs treats it as the positional terminator, and every flag after it is discarded: `[tenant-create] missing required flag(s): --slug, --name, --owner-email, --owner-name`, exit 1. I confirmed it on the locally installed pnpm 9.15.4 AND on pnpm 11.22.0, the exact version the RUNBOOK pins and the playbook tells the operator to check for. Dropping the `--` makes the identical command succeed (dry-run 'validation passed', real run 'done. tenant.id=…'). This is the only way to set billingMode, so as written the founding offer still cannot be provisioned — the same shape of defect the finding was raised for, one dash further down.

Two corroborating signs it was never executed as written: (a) the implementer's own proof line shows the command WITHOUT the `--`, i.e. they ran something other than what they wrote into the doc; (b) brief.md, changed in the same package, uses the working no-`--` form, so the two documents in one commit disagree about the command.

Minor, also worth fixing while there: the citation '(`:280-282`)' for desktop free-for-all trails 'effective-plan.service.ts:144' and reads as the same file, but free-for-all is billing.service.ts:280-282. One dash and one filename from being correct.

new_problems.issue: The impersonation fence is write-scoped and has no rule for `storage`, so an impersonating support admin can still mint a bearer credential that outlives the consented window — and because the fix deliberately keeps reads out of the tenant audit log (support-audit.interceptor.ts:182), the librarian's own log never shows it. GET /t/:slug/storage/members/<file>/signed-url returns a signed JWT link to member PII; assertMayAccess explicitly waves impersonation through (storage-demo.controller.ts:243 `if (req.impersonation) return;`), the TTL cap is 3600s for members/attachments and 86400s for covers/marc/branding, and the token is bound to tenant+ref only — nothing ties it to support_sessions. This is precisely the harm the same package fenced POST /t/:slug/exports for ('the archive would outlive this window'); the storage equivalent was missed.
new_problems.reproduction: Executed end to end (scratchpad probe3, real HTTP on a booted AppModule): library signs up, owner issues a support key, MFA-enrolled 'support'-tier admin redeems at POST /admin/support/redeem.
